questions.question: Define development and explain the difference between standard of living and quality of life.
questions.expected_answer: Development is a process of change by which the quality of life of people in a place improves over time; it can also reverse through war, disease or disaster. Standard of living refers to material wealth: income and goods and services people can afford. Quality of life is broader, including health, education, safety, housing, clean environment, human rights and freedom to choose. Development aims at quality of life; income is a means. Sen described development as expanding freedom.

questions.question: Explain the economic, social and environmental aspects of development and how they are connected.
questions.expected_answer: Economic: GDP growth, jobs, incomes, infrastructure, shift from primary to secondary, tertiary and quaternary activities. Social: health, clean water, education, housing, gender equality, rights and safety. Environmental: sustainable use of air, water, soil, forests and climate for future generations. They interact: education raises productivity; growth provides taxes for services; environmental damage such as drought or pollution harms incomes and health, especially of the poor. Good development improves all three together.

questions.question: Describe two ways of classifying countries by development and explain one limitation, with reference to South Africa.
questions.expected_answer: Developed versus developing (or MEDC/LEDC); the Brandt Line dividing a richer Global North from a poorer South; World Bank income groups (South Africa is upper-middle-income); also NICs and emerging economies such as BRICS. Limitations: labels treat a country as one unit and hide internal inequality; South Africa has a Gini coefficient of about 0,63, with wealthy Sandton beside informal settlements; they suggest one path and ignore colonial and apartheid history; countries change over time.
